niche.description:
Has your vision ever gone black when you stood up? 👇
When you stand up, gravity pulls about half a liter of blood down into your legs. For a few seconds your brain gets less blood, so your vision goes grey, then black, until sensors in your neck make your heart speed up and your veins squeeze the blood back up. Fighter pilots fight the same thing by squeezing their legs and stomach.

niche.title: What Happens When You Stand Up Too Fast?
niche.description:
Stand up too fast and your vision greys out. Here is why: gravity pulls up to a litre of blood down into your legs and belly. Less blood gets back to your heart, so the pressure feeding your brain drops. Sensors in your neck catch the drop and speed your heart up. In most healthy people it settles within about 15 seconds.

This is a general science explainer, not medical advice. If you faint or it happens a lot, see a doctor.

niche.title: Why You Shiver After You Pee?
niche.description:
Holding a very full bladder keeps part of the nervous system on alert. When you finally let go, the body flips from that alert setting towards the rest-and-digest setting, and scientists think the blood pressure can dip for a moment. The shiver may be the body's quick jolt to bring it back up, a bit like the shudder you get when you stand up too fast. It has a name, post-micturition convulsion syndrome, it happens more to men, and nobody has fully explained it yet.

outliers.description:

outliers.description:
Your body is full of fascinating features that many people overlook! From your ears to your stomach, discover interesting facts about human anatomy and how your body works.

🧠 Here are 8 fascinating body facts:

Your belly button is a scar left behind after your umbilical cord separates.
